MINUTES
  Regular Meeting Notice of the
  Gardena City Council
  Tuesday, April 26, 2022

In order to minimize the spread of the COVID 19 virus, Governor Newsom has signed Assembly
Bill 361. Please be advised that the Council Chambers are closed to the public and that some,
or all, of the Gardena City Council Members may attend this meeting telephonically.

The Regular Meeting Notice and Agenda of the Gardena City Council of the City of Gardena,
California, was called to order at 7:04 PM on Tuesday, April 26, 2022, Mayor Tasha Cerda
presiding.

1.  ROLL CALL

  Present: Mayor Tasha Cerda; Mayor Pro Tem Rodney G. Tanaka; Council Member Mark
  E. Henderson; Council Member Art Kaskanian; and Council Member Paulette C. Francis;
  Other City Officials and Employees present: City Manager Clint Osorio; City Attorney
  Carmen Vasquez; and City Clerk Mina Semenza.

  At 7:06 p.m., the City Council recessed into Closed Session via Microsoft Teams, with the
  following in attendance: Mayor Tasha Cerda; Mayor Pro Tem Rodney G. Tanaka; Council
  Member Mark E. Henderson; Council Member Art Kaskanian; Council Member Paulette C.
  Francis. Other City Officials and Employees present City Manager Clint Osorio and City
  Attorney Carmen Vasquez; Director of Community Development Greg Tsujiuchi; and
  Outside Counsel Amanda Pope.

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION - None

2.  CLOSED SESSION

   Mayor Cerda reconvened the meeting to the Regular Open Session at 8:05
  p.m., and the City Clerk noted the return of all Council Members, who were
  present at the meeting. When City Attorney Vasquez was asked if there was
  any reportable action from Closed Session, she stated that staff was
  provided with direction, but no reportable action had been taken.

3.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Courtney Preston and Kaylee Houston led the Pledge of Allegiance. Courtney and

4.  INVOCATION

  6.B  53rd Annual Municipal Clerk's Week, May 1-7, 2022

  Clerk Mina Semenza.

  6.C  "Day of Remembrance of the Armenian Genocide" - April 24, 2022

7.  APPOINTMENTS – No Appointments were made

  and Council Members Kaskanian and Francis
  Noes: None
  Absent: None

9.  EXCLUDED CONSENT CALENDAR

  8.C CITY TREASURER - Approval of Warrants/Payroll Register, April 26, 2022
  This Item was pulled by Council Members Francis and Henderson.

  Council Member Francis voiced her curiosity regarding the number of Business
  License Renewals Refunds. City Manager Osorio explained that it was done in house
  and typically refunded if forms are filled out incorrectly, these are usually staggered in
  a course of few months, but was done all at once, and that it was nothing special.
  Council Member Francis shared she received concerns from businesses on the
  3
   process and asked there was anything that can be done to streamline the system. City
  Manager Osorio responded by saying most of the complaint were on processing the
  business license renewals; we made changes inhouse by adding couple interns to help
  process the manual labor in a timely manner. He said streamlining the system is a big
  undertaking; we are limited in the process with the ERP system. He informed her that
  the system will not be supported in few years and Admin Services has did their due
  diligence by saving money on the side for the new system.

  Council Member Henderson asked City Manager Osorio if we can mail out instructions
  or create a YouTube video and post it on our website to fill out the form properly. City
  Manager said the instructions are included on the form. He said these errors are not
  unusual and they will have to recalculate and will be issued refunds. Council Member
  Henderson asked if it was worth the time to create a video. City Manager said 36 out
  of 7000 business is a minimal amount and that he will think of ways to lower the number
  of errors being made.

  8.F RECREATION & HUMAN SERVICES - Approve Amendment 02 to Local Agreement
  CCTR-1084 with the California Department of Social Services for additional funding
  of the Gardena Family Child Care Program
  This Item was pulled by Council Member Francis.

  Council Member Francis asked if it was an increase in funding and if we had to
  amend every year. She also asked if we would expand our programs and if the
  service providers get an increase also. City Manager Osorio confirmed that it is
  increase funding, programs are typically expanded, and service providers will get a
  raise, all due to inflation. Council Member Francis asked if this item would come
  back to Council. City Manager Osorio said no, it will come back if there is another
  increase.

  Public Speaker: Charisse, a childcare provider with the City of Gardena, asked
  what age range applies to $51.55 to $62.66 rate change.

  City Manager Osorio said the formulas were still being worked on and the providers
  will be contacted.

  It was moved by Council Member Francis, seconded by Mayor Cerda, and
  carried by the following roll call vote to Approve Items 8.C and 8.F:

  Ayes:  Council Member Francis, Mayor Cerda, Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka, and
  Council Members Henderson and Kaskanian
  Noes: None
  Absent: None

10. PLANNING & ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY COMMISSION ACTION SHEET

  10.A April 19, 2022 MEETING - Meeting Cancelled

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

 1. Traci Saruwatari, made all Council Members aware of the Prescription Take Back Event
  that is taking place on Saturday, April 30, 2022, from 10:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. in front of the
  Gardena Police Department. All residents are encouraged to dispose of all unused and
  expired medication.
  4
  2. Wanda Love, she expressed her concerns regarding a social media post in reference to
  the spending of public funds. She also asked about City Treasurer, Ingrid. She asked who
  is the public oversight when it comes to keeping an eye on public funds.

  City Attorney Vasquez addressed the issue with regards to City Treasurer presence; there
  is no government code or requirement unlike the elected City Councilmembers. With
  regards to the City Manager’s vehicle, it is part of City Manager’s agreement to have access
  to a city owned vehicle. City Manager Osorio addressed the question of who in the public
  is overseeing the spendings, he said approximately 60,000 residents and the five Council
  Members oversees and have access to view all the warrants. He stated that the purchases
  or leases of vehicles were not made with city tax dollars but were made with AQMD funds.

11. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS - ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES – No Items

12. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS - COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT

  12.A PUBLIC HEARING: ORDINANCE NO. 1840: Adopting Chapter 18.74 to Title 18,
  Zoning, of the Gardena Municipal Code Relating to Reasonable Accommodations
  Policy and Procedures and Directing Staff to File a Notice of Exemption from
  California Environmental Quality Act Pursuant to the Common Sense Exemption.

  ORDINANCE NO. 1840

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  GARDENA, CALIFORNIA, ADDING CHAPTER 18.74 TO TITLE 18,
  ZONING, OF THE GARDENA MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO
  REASONABLE  ACCOMMODATIONS  POLICY  AND
  PROCEDURES

  City Manager Osorio presented the Staff Report.

  Community Development Director Greg Tsujiuchi was available for any questions.

  Mayor Cerda opened the Public Hearing at 8:57 p.m. and asked if there were any
  comments from the public.

  No Public Speakers

  There was a discussion that included our City Council Members and our City Attorney.
  Some of the items discussed were which properties would receive reasonable
  accommodations, zoning codes and policies, variances for existing buildings, who
  pays for the accommodations. City Attorney Vasquez said it applies to all properties;
  we will have a procedure as being required from us to let the community know and to
  assist them; costs for the accommodations can be worked between the landlord and
  the tenants. City Attorney Vasquez shared the Ordinance will be posted on our
  website and forms will be available at CDD.

  There was no further comment, Mayor Cerda closed the Public Hearing at 9:01
  p.m.

  Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka introduced Ordinance No. 1840.

  5
   It was moved by Council Member Kaskanian, seconded by Council Member
  Francis, and carried by the following roll call vote to approve the
  Introduction of Ordinance No. 1840:

  Ayes:  Council Members Kaskanian and Francis, Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka,
  Council Member Henderson, and Mayor Cerda
  Noes: None
  Absent: None

13. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS - ELECTED & CITY MANAGER'S OFFICES

  13.A Financial Transparency Dashboard

  City Manager Osorio presented a Power Point.

  City Manager shared they only spent $300 in putting together the dashboard and
  commended Khoi Quach. The entire Council gave kudos to the Finance
  Department.

  13.B COVID-19 Update

  City Manager Osorio presented the update.

14. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS – POLICE

  14.A PUBLIC HEARING: ORDINANCE NO. 1841, Adopting a Military Equipment Use
  Policy of the City of Gardena, California Governing the Use of Military Equipment
  pursuant to Assembly Bill 481

  ORDINANCE NO. 1841

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  GARDENA, CALIFORNIA, ADOPTING A MILITARY EQUIPMENT
  USE POLICY OF THE CITY OF GARDENA, CALIFORNIA
  GOVERNING THE USE OF MILITARY EQUIPMENT PURSUANT
  TO ASSEMBLY BILL 481

  City Manager Osorio presented the Staff Report.

  Police Chief Mike Saffell and Captain Osorio were available for any questions.

  Mayor Cerda opened the Public Hearing at 9:16 p.m. and asked if there were any
  comments from the public.

  Police Chief Mike Saffell presented a PowerPoint presentation.

  Public Speakers:

  Sherelle Diggs, voiced her concerns about military equipment, and said we need to
  start thinking about people and not hardness. She asked if we had no-knock warrants.

  Police Chief Mike Saffell said we do not utilize no-knock warrants in the City of
  Gardena. He also informed about the services offered by the police department and
  clarified the different types of equipment and their uses.
  6
   There was a discussion that included our Mayor, Council Members and City
  Attorney. Some of the items discussed were Council Member Kaskanian asked
  about which Assembly member introduced this item; if we need to be transparent
  about the inventory and if it was logical; consequences of not being transparent;
  do we budget to purchase guns or equipment every year. Police Chief Saffell
  responded that there are big concerns in doing so; said he has resources to
  replenish as needed. City Attorney stated that if we do not adopt the policy, it will
  prohibit the police department from using any of the equipment. Council Member
  Francis said when she thinks of military equipment, she thinks of war; asked about
  the policy if not adopted; the source of purchase; possession of equipment from
  the list on AB481; training component; complaints and its process; annual report
  on the weapons; audits; and if other mutual agencies need to have the same
  Ordinance. Chief Saffell answered all her questions. Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka said
  we not only need to protect our personnel, but our personnel need to have the right
  equipment to protect our community; gave a history of Gardena Police Department
  with the use of the equipment and how they were used in a proper manner. Council
  Member Henderson asked about mutual aid; he suggested updating older
  equipment; said he appreciated the report. Captain Osorio added explanation
  regarding the budget.

  There was no further comment, Mayor Cerda closed the Public Hearing at 9:52
  p.m.

  Council Member Henderson introduced Ordinance No. 1841.

  It was moved by Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka, seconded by Council Member
  Henderson, and carried by the following roll call vote to approve the
  Introduction of Ordinance No. 1841:

  Ayes:  Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka, Council Members Henderson, Kaskanian and
  Francis, and Mayor Cerda
  Noes: None
  Absent: None

15. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS - PUBLIC WORKS

  15.A Approve Consultation Contract for HF&H Consultants, LLC to Monitor the Solid
  Waste Contract and Manage Senate Bill 1383 Requirements for the City of
  Gardena.

  City Manager Osorio presented the Staff Report.

  Director of Public Works Allan Rigg, was available for any questions.

  Council Member Kaskanian asked if we would pay out of pocket and if we need a
  consultant company. City Manager Osorio answered no we do not pay out of pocket
  and the consultant is needed to oversee WRG. Council Member Francis asked if we
  contracted with them before; if it includes 3% raise every January; about reports that

  7
   will be generated; education and assistance for others; staff vs. consultant. City
  Manager, City Attorney and Consultant Debbie Morris answered Council Member
  Francis’s questions. Mayor Cerda said it will be a learning experience.

  It was moved by Council Member Kaskanian, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem
  Tanaka, and by the following vote to Approve Consulting Contract:

  Ayes:  Council Member Kaskanian, Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka, Council
  Members Henderson and Francis, and Mayor Cerda
  Noes: None
  Absent: None

  2) She is concerned about the Covid-19 cases among our staff and asked what our safety
